{{Legend0|#D3D3D3|No election}} }} The '''2027 United States gubernatorial elections''' are scheduled to be held on November 2, 2027, in the states of [[Kentucky]] and [[Mississippi]], as well as an election in [[Louisiana]] on October 9, 2027.{{Efn|If no candidate receives a majority in the Louisiana primary, a runoff between the top two finishers will be held on November 20.}} In addition, special elections may take place (depending on state law) if other gubernatorial seats are vacated. These elections form part of the [[2027 United States elections]]. The last regular gubernatorial elections for all three states were in [[2023 United States gubernatorial elections|2023]]. == Partisan composition == Going into this election, there are 30 [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] governors and 20 [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governors in the United States. Democrats hold one governorship up for election in a state that [[Donald Trump]] won in 2024 (Kentucky). He is eligible to run for re-election but has not stated if he will do so. ==Mississippi== {{Main|2027 Mississippi gubernatorial election}} Governor [[Tate Reeves]] was re-elected in [[2023 Mississippi gubernatorial election|2023]] with 50.9% of the vote. He is [[Term limits in the United States|term-limited]] by the [[Constitution of Mississippi|Mississippi Constitution]] and cannot seek re-election to a third term.{{cite news |last1=Harrison |first1=Bobby |title=How a Tate Reeves victory would place him in Mississippi history books |url=https://mississippitoday.org/2023/10/27/tate-reeves-history-books/ |access-date=November 8, 2023 |work=[[Mississippi Today]] |date=October 27, 2023}} Democratic nominee in 2023 and former [[Mississippi Public Service Commission]]er [[Brandon Presley]] was seen as a potential candidate but ultimately announced in November 2026 that he would not run.{{cite news |last1=Vance |first1=Taylor |title=Presley says he won’t run for governor in ’27 |url=https://mississippitoday.org/2026/11/27/presley-not-running-governor-mississippi/ |access-date=November 27, 2026 |work=[[Mississippi Today]] |date=November 27, 2026}} ==See also== *[[List of elections in 2027]] ==Notes== {{Notelist}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{United States gubernatorial elections}} {{2027 United States elections}} {{DEFAULTSORT:United States Gubernatorial Elections, 2027}} [[Category:2027 United States gubernatorial elections| ]]

The '''2027 Louisiana gubernatorial election''' will be held on October 9, 2027, to elect the [[governor of Louisiana]]. If no candidate receives a majority in the primary, a runoff between the top two finishers will be held on November 20. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Jeff Landry]] is eligible to seek a second term.

==Background==
Gubernatorial elections in Louisiana use a [[two-round system]]. If no candidate receives a majority in the primary, a runoff between the top two finishers (among all candidates, without consideration of political party) will be held on November 20.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2027 Elections|url=https://www.sos.la.gov/media/byfpyc5f/elections-calendar-2027.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918031735/https://www.sos.la.gov/media/byfpyc5f/elections-calendar-2027.pdf|archive-date=September 18, 2026|publisher=[[Louisiana Secretary of State]]|access-date=September 30, 2026}}</ref>

Louisiana is considered to be a stronghold for the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=LaRose |first1=Greg |title=Republicans take lead in Louisiana registered voters; Democrats claim purge |url=https://lailluminator.com/2026/07/07/republican-voter-louisiana/ |website=Louisiana Illuminator |access-date=November 26, 2026 |date=July 7, 2026}}</ref> Despite this, [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] in Louisiana consider the 2027 gubernatorial election a promising opportunity for their party in the state; especially after the unexpectedly-close performance in [[2026 United States Senate election in Louisiana|the 2026 U.S. Senate election in the state]] by their of their nominee, [[Jamie Davis (politician)|Jamie Davis]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hutchinson |first1=Piper |title=Louisiana Democrats’ near-miss on Senate seat gives party hope for governor’s race |url=https://lailluminator.com/2026/11/05/louisiana-democrats-near-miss-on-senate-seat-gives-party-hope-for-governors-race/ |website=Louisiana Illuminator |access-date=November 26, 2026 |date=November 5, 2026}}</ref>

===Term limits amendment===
{{main|2026 Louisiana Amendment 4}}

In November 2026, Louisiana voters approved a constitutional change which amended the gubernatorial [[term limit]]s provision in the [[Constitution of Louisiana]]. Previously, the constitution had only capped the number of consecutive terms at two. The amendment, however, imposes a lifetime limit of two gubernatorial terms. This change does not have a [[grandfather clause]], and therefore counts terms served before its ratification. As a result, living past two-term governors [[John Bel Edwards]] (a Democrat) and [[Bobby Jindal]] (Republican) have been rendered ineligible to seek another term. Under the previous constitutional clause, either would have been legally eligible to run for a non-consecutive third term in 2027.<ref name="nola">{{cite web|last=Faucheux|first=Ron|date=October 24, 2026|title=Ron Faucheux: For Louisiana governors, two terms and you’re out?|url=https://www.nola.com/opinions/ron_faucheux/governors-term-limits-landry-edwards-amendment/article_e0d2e136-2364-4991-a657-8f9ce4772f8d.html|website=nola.com|access-date=October 27, 2026}}</ref>
